subject: Cloud Computing
title: Security Incident Response
description: A quick win: understand Security Incident Response.

hook.text: Your monitoring alerts fire at 3 AM: unusual data export from a production database. What do you do first?

buildup.text: An incident response plan defines who does what when a breach happens: contain, investigate, communicate.

discovery.text: Cloud adds unique challenges: you can't physically seize a server. Evidence exists as logs and snapshots.

twist.text: Most teams freeze during incidents. Without practice, the plan stays on paper while damage spreads.

climax.text: Regular tabletop exercises — simulated incidents — prepare teams so the real thing isn't their first rodeo.

punchline.text: A plan you've never practiced is just a document. Practice it.

quiz.question: Why are tabletop exercises important for incident response?
options: They prepare teams through simulated incidents so real events aren't their first experience
They replace the need for monitoring and alerting systems
They are legally required before deploying any cloud service

details.summary: Cloud incident response follows a structured process: preparation, detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned. Cloud-specific challenges include multi-account investigation, ephemeral resources, and the need for pre-configured forensic tooling.
details.whyItMatters: Breaches are inevitable; response speed determines impact. Organizations that practice incident response in cloud environments recover faster and suffer less damage.
takeaways: Follow a structured process from detection to lessons learned
Pre-configure forensic tools before incidents occur
Ephemeral cloud resources require proactive log collection

faq.question: How does cloud incident response differ from traditional?
faq.answer: Cloud environments lack physical access for forensics, resources may be destroyed by auto-scaling, and investigation spans multiple services and accounts. Pre-configured logging, snapshot capabilities, and isolated forensic accounts are essential for effective cloud incident response.

faq.question: What should an incident response plan include?
faq.answer: Defined roles and escalation paths, contact information, pre-approved containment actions, forensic tooling setup, communication templates, log retention policies, and regular tabletop exercises. The plan must be tested and updated at least annually.
